security.title: Security Posture
security.zero_disk_desc: No persistence. All cryptographic materials and payloads are strictly confined to volatile RAM, ensuring total forensic deniability.
security.zeroize_desc: Physical memory allocations are actively zeroized explicitly after dispatch or TTL expiry.
security.dpop_desc: All payloads enforce RFC 9449 standard. Rogue network transitions immediately freeze outbound transport layer.

features.title: Secure Native Integration
features.desc: Unlike other NPM libraries that keep cryptographic material exposed in the JS garbage collector memory, Sovereign SDK operates a native C++ engine that destroys the material using SecureZeroMemory immediately after signing the transaction.
features.f1_desc: We use JSI to execute crypto-operations at the C++ level, avoiding the JS bridge.
features.f2_desc: No key ever touches Disk. Generated in RAM, used, and wiped in milliseconds.
features.f3_desc: Asymmetric signatures tied to the physical device. Stealing the Bearer token is useless without the private key.
features.bullet3: Synchronous communication via React Native Nitro / JSI

architecture.title: Core Security Architecture
architecture.subtitle: Based on 5 fundamental pillars to protect transaction integrity under a volatile and hostile memory environment.
architecture.p1_desc: Requests are serialized to binary and queued in a static C++ ledger in physical memory. Each block is cryptographically linked with SHA-256.
architecture.p2_desc: Active erasure using std::fill and SecureZeroMemory immediately after dispatch or TTL expiration to prevent leaks to the JS Heap.
architecture.p3_desc: Background engine that detects dynamic manipulation (injection or memory corruption). Freezes execution and preserves evidence.
architecture.p4_desc: Ephemeral generation and signing of Proofs of Possession (DPoP - RFC 9449) using WebCrypto to avoid overloading the C++ core.
architecture.p5_desc: Decoupled from the network via the Command pattern. Native adapters for Fetch, Axios or GraphQL included.
architecture.p6_desc: Native support for fallback engine without JSI. Ideal for CI/CD pipelines, web and component testing without real hardware.

flow.title: In-Memory Operational Flow
flow.intro: The runtime lifecycle of a secure request follows a strict flow to ensure cryptographic resilience:
flow.step1: The application (App) invokes executeRequest() on the SovereignClientCore.
flow.step2: Memory integrity is verified. If the Ledger has been compromised (e.g. code injection or memory dump), an IntegrityBreachError is immediately thrown.
flow.step3: If the environment is safe, network connection is checked:
flow.step3_online: Online: The ephemeral DPoP proof is attached and the request is dispatched to the NetworkAdapter. Upon success, hardware secure erasure (SecureZeroMemory) is executed on the buffers to leave no trace in memory, and the response is returned.
flow.step3_offline: Offline or HTTP 503: The request is queued in the volatile ledger (MemoryQueue). The C++ core cryptographically links the payload using SHA-256 chaining (hash $H_n$) and initiates a zeroize of temporary variables, returning a pending Promise to the application that will automatically resolve on reconnection.
